bullets.title: ORCL Q4: Strong bookings but capex overhangs; stock -8-10% AH
bullets.body: Oracle FQ4 beat estimates (EPS $2.11 vs $1.96, revenue $19.18B vs $19.10B) and RPO surged to $638B (+363% YoY, up $85B q/q) on four $8B+ AI contracts. The negative reaction came from FY27 capex guidance of $90-95B gross (~$70B net cash after $20-25B customer prepayments), a planned $40B debt/equity raise including $20B ATM, and negative free cash flow of -$23.7B in FY26. FY27 revenue reiterated at $90B; Cloud guided +57-64% constant currency. Bulls point to $75B of BYOH/prepaid RPO reducing net capex and a new CFO seen as more credible; bears cite margin compression and balance sheet risk.

bullets.title: ADBE Q2 beat but organic ARR cut, CFO departs, freemium pivot—stock down 15-20%
bullets.body: Adobe beat Q2 (revenue $6.62B, EPS $5.96), but cut FY26 organic ARR guidance by ~$480M-$500M to reflect a strategic pivot toward freemium/user acquisition over near-term monetization, and deferred Creative Cloud pricing. CFO Dan Durn departed to join Marvell as CFO effective June 15, leaving Adobe without both a CEO and CFO. Sell-side mostly held ratings but cut PTs 10-15%; Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform, Evercore to In Line, Stifel to Hold. Consensus sees risk of ARR drifting to mid-single digits. AI-first ARR tripled YoY to >$500M but still <2% of total.

bullets.title: AMD upgraded to Buy at Citi ($575 PT): GPU upside at Meta not priced in
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Neutral to Buy with a $575 PT (raised from $460), citing AMD's emerging as a legitimate second GPU source for Meta's 6 GW, 4-year AI infrastructure deal. Each GW translates to ~$15B revenue for AMD. Citi estimates CY26/27/28 EPS 12-13% above Street; AI revenue forecast at $33B in 2027 (up 137% YoY) and $50.8B in 2028. CPU TAM expanded to $137B by 2030 (36% CAGR). Also noted: AMD claims 15/15 top spots on Amazon CPU bestseller list.

bullets.title: INTC double-upgraded to Buy at BofA ($135 PT) on hyperscaler packaging and foundry optionality
bullets.body: BofA double-upgraded Intel from Underperform to Buy and raised its PT to $135 from $96, citing Intel's EMIB advanced packaging win with Google for TPU production and Intel's improved foundry competitive position against TSMC capacity constraints. INTC traded +25% in the week. JPMorgan's note from Chips for Breakfast also flagged that TSMC leading-edge nodes are running at 110-120% utilization with no relief until 2027-28, structurally benefiting Intel foundry. KOSPI semiconductor stocks also surged on AI demand.

bullets.title: AVGO: XPV platform targets $130-190B CY28 revenue from Anthropic/OpenAI ASICs; stock volatile
bullets.body: AVGO partners with Apollo/Blackstone to launch the $35B XPV AI compute platform targeting OpenAI and Anthropic GPU ASICs. The 20 GW platform implies ~13 GW of ASIC shipments by CY28 at $10-15B/GW, potentially $130-190B in revenue from these two customers alone—plus $73B from Google TPUs and $20B from Meta. UBS reiterates Buy at $485 but notes back-end supply constraints (EMIB v9 packaging issues) and Mediatek share gains at Google as near-term risks. AVGO remains JPMorgan's top pick in semis.

bullets.title: NVDA: CPO/800V delay narrative pressured stock; management denies delays
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis reported CPO (co-packaged optics for scale-up) and 800V HVDC power delays, triggering a ~12% sector selloff in optical/AI infrastructure names. Nvidia's Networking SVP and CEO Jensen Huang subsequently denied the delays at Computex, saying scale-out and scale-up CPO timelines are confirmed; Lumentum confirmed CPO switch mix >50% for Nvidia. Morgan Stanley maintained its $10B optical engine forecast for 2027 at 6-7M units vs. investor expectations of 20-30M—suggesting the 'delay' narrative is primarily about investor expectations being too bullish, not NVDA product slippage. NVDA stock flat for ~10 months despite AI boom.

bullets.title: GOOGL: TPU v10 may use Samsung 2nm, Google backs Anthropic $35B chip deal
bullets.body: Google is discussing using Samsung Foundry's 2nm process for the I/O die of its next-gen Icefish TPU (v10), per The Information, reducing TSMC dependency. Separately, Google is providing financial backing for Anthropic's $35B chip securitization with Broadcom. Wolfe's cloud analyst raised GCP revenue growth forecast to 81% in 2026 (vs. Street 63%), noting Anthropic accounts for 25-30% of GCP revenue in 2027-28. Google also rolled out Gemini AI upgrades in Chrome globally and launched new AI Search ad formats at Cannes.

bullets.title: MSFT Xbox explores spinoff, plans major layoffs; restricts Claude Fable
bullets.body: Microsoft Xbox is planning major layoffs post-June 30 fiscal year-end amid operating margin issues (~3% margin, nearly $500M annual revenue decline excluding ABK). Microsoft has not ruled out spinning off Xbox. Microsoft also restricted internal employee use of Claude Fable (Anthropic's new Mythos-class model) over data retention concerns.

bullets.title: META: EU orders WhatsApp to give rival AI chatbots free access; Manus deal unwound by China
bullets.body: EU antitrust regulators ordered Meta to allow competing AI chatbots unrestricted, free access to WhatsApp within five days, citing competition in the AI chatbot market. Meta plans to challenge the order. Separately, China's NDRC blocked Meta's ~$2B Manus AI acquisition; Meta has ceased data-sharing and is sunsetting the unit. Meta is planning a 168 MW AI data center in India via Reliance.

bullets.title: ROKU: reportedly exploring sale, streaming gatekeeper thesis
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Roku is in talks with at least one U.S. media company about a potential sale, with shares jumping 20%+. Multiple analysts and commentators see Fox, Netflix, and Comcast as potential suitors. Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on Roku's new home screen. The broader question framed by analysts is which company becomes streaming's gatekeeper.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: DoJ approves Paramount-WBD merger; California AG could still block
bullets.body: DoJ approved Paramount Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros without conditions or divestitures. Australian regulators also cleared the deal. However, California AG Rob Bonta is still reviewing and could sue to block the transaction. Paramount is also reportedly seeking to sublicense NRL rights in Australia via a Foxtel-Amazon structure.

bullets.title: DKNG: prediction markets driving re-rating; CEO confident no OSB cannibalization
bullets.body: DKNG's May annualized prediction market volumes reached $3.1B (+34% M/M), with consumer volume +24% M/M. CEO at Jefferies conference refuted cannibalization concerns, noting handle declines come from 'sharps' moving to prediction markets (net-positive for margins). CFTC released expansive prediction market rules allowing sports bets. DKNG targeting 30%+ long-term EBITDA margins; expects $1B+ EBITDA in FY26. Wells Fargo raised 2028+ estimates and TAM assumptions for both DKNG and Flutter.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi Buy at $225 PT; AIPCon10 takeaways positive; CEO warns against using AI as layoff excuse
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on PLTR ($225 PT, 71.7% upside) after CFO meeting highlighting strong AIP momentum, normalization of USG bookings post-Middle East conflict, and new customer wins including Kirkland & Ellis and N-scale neocloud clients. Baird reiterated Outperform at $200 following AIPCon 10. CEO Alex Karp said executives who use AI to justify mass layoffs are 'full of shit.'

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory LTAs locking 2027-2028 capacity; HBM pricing +40% in CY27
bullets.body: Wolfe raised MU PT to $1,250 (from $550) on memory pricing momentum: DRAM ASP up 35% Q/Q in C2Q with another 15% in 3Q guided, NAND similar trajectory. CSPs have locked up 2027 memory LTAs and are already moving to secure 2028 supply. HBM pricing expected to rise 40% YoY in CY27 on LTA mix and HBM4/4E adoption. JPMorgan raised STX and WDC PTs on similar logic. SK Hynix plans US Nasdaq listing by August and tripling wafer capacity by 2034.

bullets.title: ANET raised to $190 PT at MS and JPM; 1.6T platform launch confirms networking leadership
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan both raised ANET PTs to $190 on AI front-end networking TAM expansion. ANET launched its 1.6T rack-scale AI networking portfolio (Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 products) in partnership with Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle. Dell'Oro estimates AI front-end networking to grow from $1.8B (2025) to $6.3B (2030) at 29% CAGR; Morgan Stanley sees upside to $10B. ANET also confirmed CISCO raised to $130 PT at Morgan Stanley on AI pipeline visibility.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: CPO timeline debate; management confirms ramps on schedule despite SemiAnalysis FUD
bullets.body: LITE CEO confirmed at Mizuho conference that CPO scale-up products will ship H2 2027 with formal ramp in 2028—no delays. He also noted that NPO opportunity is 'frankly bigger than CPO.' COHR confirmed record bookings and that CY27 is effectively booked out, with NVDA's equity investment confirmed. Multiple sell-side analysts (JPMorgan, MS, Morgan Stanley) view the optical pullback as overdone. LITE/COHR trade at <1x PEG at 25x CY28 earnings on 40%+ EPS growth.

bullets.title: AMZN: $17.5B term loan facility; expands LTL freight to compete with truckers
bullets.body: Amazon secured a $17.5B delayed-draw term loan facility led by Citigroup to fund AI-driven capex expansion. Amazon also launched a less-than-truckload freight service nationally for all businesses, which pressured ODFL (-6%), SAIA (-7%), XPO (-4%), and FDXF (-6%) on the day. AWS Graviton5 (custom CPU) announced as generally available with 25% performance improvement and 192 cores.

bullets.title: NET: Investor Day raises margins, $5B+ revenue target; stock +1.5% post-event
bullets.body: Cloudflare raised its long-term operating margin target to 30%+ (from 20%+), FCF margin to 30-35%, and set a $5B+ annualized revenue target before end of 2028. Rule of 50 North Star metric raised. 78% of leading AI companies run on Cloudflare; AI agent traffic up 1,700%+ YoY. Wolfe raised ZS PT to $150 from $183 (incrementally more positive on AI security demand) though BTIG raised Cloudflare PT to $269. Morgan Stanley reiterated OW on ANET and CSCO on inference-driven networking.

bullets.title: SPOT: 2026 Spring Training survey shows dominance; Reserved and AI features drive pricing power
bullets.body: KeyBanc survey shows Spotify at 42% adoption among audio consumers with 2x nearest competitor, lowest cancellation intent (18%) for second consecutive quarter. 53% of listeners interested in AI remix feature with 39% willing to pay $5/mo; 58% interested in Spotify Fitness; 46% interested in personal podcasts. Citi maintains Buy at $620; analyst raises estimates on Audiobooks+, Marketplace, and geographic mix clarity.

bullets.title: GEV: Morgan Stanley data center check negative; power turbine pricing durable but orders expected lower in 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's report on GEV notes that gas turbine industry orders are expected to decline in 2027 vs. 2026 levels (~117GW). However, 22V Research field checks on power infrastructure show strong and durable pricing momentum lasting several years for large-frame turbines. KKR launched Helix Digital ($10B+) with GEV's Vistra and Nvidia as partners.
